analysis.summary:
## Biggest Storylines

- **Several teams are showing the same draft philosophy in different forms: stay flexible, trust the board, and think beyond Year 1.**  
  That was the clearest thread from the Eagles, Panthers, Ravens, and Giants. Baltimore’s Eric DeCosta said the Ravens still intend to lean **best player available** with **11 picks starting at No. 14**. Carolina’s **Dan Morgan** said the Panthers feel **“in a good spot”** and are ready for **“all scenarios”** at **No. 19**. Philadelphia’s **Howie Roseman** said he thinks about missed first-round picks every day and is focusing on what a player can become by **Year 3**, not just rookie production. The common message: teams with real draft capital are resisting the urge to force a need pick.

- **The Eagles’ receiver situation remains the most interesting public roster subplot, even if Roseman is trying to keep it calm.**  
  Philadelphia’s trade for **Dontayvion Wicks** has only fueled outside speculation about **A.J. Brown**, but Roseman kept his stance unchanged publicly. At the same time, he said the Eagles are **not making major changes** to how they evaluate offensive linemen despite the offseason coaching shift around **Jeff Stoutland**. That combination matters: the Eagles are still operating like a team planning multiple layers ahead, not reacting emotionally to short-term noise. The Brown chatter is still just that — chatter — but it won’t go away until the draft passes.

- **Las Vegas is telegraphing a quarterback plan that could reshape both the rookie class and its own offense.**  
  The Raiders have added **Kirk Cousins** as a veteran stabilizer under new head coach **Klint Kubiak**, and **John Spytek** said he wants the coaches to “sleep a little better at night” with that kind of experience in the room. At the same time, the Raiders are saying **“best guy will play”** between **Fernando Mendoza** and Cousins in training camp. Teams have reportedly called about the **No. 1 pick**, but the current read is that Las Vegas is locked in on Mendoza. That creates a pretty clean structure: veteran floor from Cousins, rookie upside from Mendoza, and a public stance that still leaves the camp battle open.

- **The Giants have two major draft/roster tracks running at once: the Dexter Lawrence standoff and a very open-minded pick at No. 5.**  
  **Joe Schoen** said talks with **Dexter Lawrence’s** reps have been **good** and **productive** over the last 5–6 days, and the team wants him to stay. Separately, Schoen said the Giants have watched a lot of **Ohio State** defensive film and described **Jeremiyah Love** as an **offensive weapon**, not just a running back. That suggests New York is still sorting out whether its first pick is a defensive anchor or a versatile offensive piece. Lawrence’s status raises the stakes, but it does not appear to have forced a deadline or a public ultimatum.

## Team / Offseason Signals

- **Eagles: roster construction is still about sequencing, not instant gratification.**  
  Roseman’s comments about evaluating players for what they can be in **Year 3** line up with the broader Eagles model: they are not drafting purely for immediate rookie snaps, and they are not signaling any major philosophical shift even after the offensive line coaching transition. The **Dontayvion Wicks** trade adds a real roster piece, but the bigger signal is that Philadelphia keeps looking for long-range fits while publicly refusing to move off **A.J. Brown** talk.

- **Panthers: the board appears to matter more than the position label.**  
  Morgan’s “no rule against” using a first-round pick on a receiver for the **third straight year** is the kind of comment that keeps everyone guessing, but his bigger point was that the Panthers feel ready for every scenario at **No. 19**. His note that **Bryce Young’s fifth-year option** will be handled **after the draft** also suggests Carolina is keeping its quarterback process separate from the immediate draft decision. The reference to **age and injuries** as factors reinforces that this is a board-based evaluation, not a simple position-based one.

- **Ravens: classic Baltimore flexibility is still intact.**  
  With **11 picks** and the first one at **No. 14**, DeCosta has the kind of draft room that can absorb value wherever it falls. CIN.summary:
The Cincinnati Bengals’ biggest roster question today is pass rush. Paul Dehner Jr. framed the issue as whether the Bengals have done enough this offseason, and the answer appears to hinge on next week’s NFL Draft. The front office has not fully closed the gap, so edge help remains a clear roster priority and a signal of how aggressively Cincinnati plans to address a unit that still needs reinforcement.

There was also a small but relevant roster loss: Cameron Sample left the Bengals for the San Francisco 49ers as an unrestricted free agent. His departure adds to the need for depth on the defensive front. What to watch next: whether Cincinnati uses premium draft capital on a pass rusher, which would be the clearest sign the coaching staff and front office view this as a must-fix area.

SF.summary:
The San Francisco 49ers are using the pre-draft stretch to probe two roster areas: wide receiver and the offensive line. Omar Cooper visited on Wednesday, signaling the team is still evaluating additions for the receiver room, though his fit and draft standing are not specified. At the same time, The Athletic’s Vic Tafur noted the 49ers have a hole at left guard and a future need at left tackle, but history suggests they are unlikely to address those spots early, pointing instead to mid-round options.

The 49ers also signed Cameron Sample as an unrestricted free agent from the Bengals, adding another body to the roster. The combined moves suggest San Francisco is prioritizing depth and developmental options, with next steps likely tied to whether they lean on mid-round draft picks to patch the offensive line.

That move still fuels speculation about Brown’s long-term role, but Roseman did not indicate a shift in direction. He also reinforced that the Eagles’ draft model remains focused on what a player can become by Year 3, not just rookie help, while saying the club is not making major changes to how it evaluates offensive linemen despite Jeff Stoutland’s departure.  

Roseman also acknowledged his occasional first-round misses and said any issues with Jalen Hurts are handled directly. The broader takeaway: Philadelphia is projecting patience and continuity in its roster-building, but the wide receiver situation remains the clearest spot to watch next.

NYG.summary:
The New York Giants’ biggest storyline today is the uneasy Dexter Lawrence II contract situation. ESPN reported an impasse in extension talks, while Joe Schoen said the Giants have had “good” and “productive” conversations with Lawrence’s reps over the past 5–6 days and want him back. Lawrence is not participating in the offseason program as he seeks a trade, which raises real roster and leadership questions for the defense if the standoff lingers.

On the draft front, Schoen said the Giants have watched a lot of Ohio State defensive film, signaling heavy pre-draft work on that pipeline with the No. 5 pick approaching. He also described Jeremiyah Love as an “offensive weapon,” not just a running back, hinting the Giants are considering versatile skill talent. What happens next: resolve the Lawrence situation, then narrow the fifth-overall board.

LV.summary:
The Las Vegas Raiders’ quarterback plan is taking shape around two tracks: veteran stability and a likely franchise rookie. General manager John Spytek said Kirk Cousins was added to help establish how new head coach Klint Kubiak wants the offense to work, and Spytek said Cousins should help coaches “sleep a little better at night.” At the same time, the Raiders will let Fernando Mendoza and Cousins compete in camp, with the Week 1 starter labeled as “the best guy.”  

That lines up with the bigger signal around the No. 1 pick: teams have inquired about trading for it, but Spytek said those teams “know where they stand,” and it seems a certainty the Raiders will draft Mendoza. The next watch item is how quickly Mendoza separates himself in camp.
